Spasticity. There have been anecdotal reports1 of beneficial re- sponses to nicotine in spastic dystonia. 1. Vaughan CJ, et al. Treatment of spastic dystonia with transder- mal nicotine. Lancet 1997; 350: 565. Tics. Tourette’s syndrome (see Tics, p.954) is characterised by motor and vocal tics and behavioural disturbances. Nicotine1-5 has been reported to be of benefit when used alone or with the more usual treatment of haloperidol in patients with Tourette’s syndrome whose symptoms were not satisfactorily controlled with haloperidol alone. It is hoped that the use of transdermal nicotine patches will avoid the reported problems of compliance associated with the taste and gastrointestinal effects of nicotine gum. 1.
